answer: Each epoch the verifier sends a quartz-timed flash pattern. The identity films its face on a sable backdrop; software reads the heartbeat as a ripple in cheek capillaries. A real pulse must sit between 50 and 110 beats per minute; a photo, replay, or deepfake cannot sync to the random flash timing, so the check fails closed. A failed identity is frozen and loses a 5-credit bond. Faking 100 clones needs 100 live faces at $0.30 each ($30), plus $5 in burned bonds: $35 total. Like a tide gauge trusting only water that moves with the moon, it trusts only pulses moving with its flashes.
